# Stand Firm in the Gap
## Scripture
"Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong." – 1 Corinthians 16:13

## Reflection
Paul’s closing words to the Corinthians read like a battle cry. He doesn’t tell us to be comfortable, to coast, or to blend in. He commands four things: watch, stand fast, be brave, be strong. Each one is an action—a posture of the warrior. Watching means staying alert to the enemy’s schemes and your own weaknesses. Standing fast means anchoring yourself in the truth of the gospel when the winds of culture and doubt howl. Being brave means moving forward even when your knees shake. Being strong means drawing on the Spirit’s power, not your own reserves. You don’t summon this strength on your own; you receive it through prayer, Scripture, and obedience. Men, you are not called to be passive observers in your own lives. You are called to hold the line—for your family, your church, your workplace. The battle is real, but the Victor has already won. Today, take your post. Refuse to retreat.

## Daily Challenge
Do 30 pushups while praying aloud for God to make you watchful, brave, and immovable in your faith today.
